Rashi on Niddah 56a:10:1.hebrew: זבוגי - פרוי"ט הנמצאים יבשים במחוזא, והוא צב, ויש שקורין אותו בלע"ז בו"ט:
Rashi on Niddah 56a:10:1.english: Zevugei - [These are] froit [toads] that are found dried in Meḥoza. And it is the tzav, and there are those who call it in Old French bot [toad].

Rashi on Niddah 56a:14:1.hebrew: רר - כעין ריר שהוא לח, כמו (שמואל א כ״א:י״ד) ויורד רירו על זקנו:
Rashi on Niddah 56a:14:1.english: Runs - Like rir [spittle], which is moist, as [in the verse] (I Samuel 21:14): "and let his spittle run down upon his beard."

Rashi on Niddah 56a:16:1.hebrew: תחילתו אע"פ שאין סופו - אין צריך שיהו המים פושרין בסוף, כשיכלה מעת לעת:
Rashi on Niddah 56a:16:1.english: Its beginning, even though not its end - It is not necessary for the water to be lukewarm at the end, when the twenty-four-hour period concludes.

Rashi on Niddah 56a:17:1.hebrew: יהודה בן נקוסא אומר - אין צריך שיהו המים פושרין בסוף, אכן יהו על השרץ כמעת לעת, אע"פ שאין סופן. וקולא היא, דאי לא הדר בהכי טהור, ואע"ג דאי הוו פושרין כל מעת לעת הוה הדר:
Rashi on Niddah 56a:17:1.english: Yehuda ben Nekosa says - It is not necessary that the water be lukewarm at the end; rather, it must be on the creeping animal for a twenty-four-hour period, even though at the end [the water] is not [lukewarm]. And this is a leniency, for if it does not return [to its moist state] through this [soaking], it is ritually pure, even though if [the water] had been lukewarm for the entire twenty-four-hour period, it would have returned.

Rashi on Niddah 56a:18:1.english: The impurity of decayed flesh - A full ladleful of it transmits impurity through contact, carrying, and a tent.

Rashi on Niddah 56a:1:1.hebrew: ממקום טומאה - ממקום שזובו יוצא, שהוא טמא בשבילו:
Rashi on Niddah 56a:1:1.english: From a place of impurity - From the place from which his discharge issues, on account of which he is impure.

Rashi on Niddah 56a:21:1.hebrew: ומטמא בין לח ובין יבש - הכתם או השרץ, בין שנמצאו לחין, בין שנמצאו יבשין, מטמא כל טהרות שנמצאו במבוי מיום כיבודו, ושעשתה האשה מיום כבוס:
Rashi on Niddah 56a:21:1.english: And it renders impure whether moist or dry - The stain or the creeping animal, whether they were found moist or they were found dry, renders impure all pure items that were found in the alleyway from the day of its sweeping, and [those] that the woman prepared from the day of laundering.

Rashi on Niddah 56a:21:2.hebrew: היבש מטמא למפרע - עד שעת כיבוד או כיבוס, דאיכא למימר: לאחר כיבוס מיד נפל. אבל הלח אינו מטמא למפרע אלא עד שעה שנוכל לומר: אם נפל באותו יום, עדיין הוא יכול להיות עכשיו לח. אבל עד שעת הכיבוד לזמן מרובה – לא, דהא לח הוא, ואי מההיא שעתא נפל, הוה מתעביד יבש:
Rashi on Niddah 56a:21:2.english: The dry [one] renders [items] impure retroactively - Until the time of sweeping or laundering, as it can be said that it fell immediately after laundering. But the moist [one] does not render [items] impure retroactively except until the time when we can say: If it fell on that day, it could still be moist now. But [retroactively] until the time of sweeping, for a long period of time – no, for it is moist, and had it fallen from that time, it would have become dry.

Rashi on Niddah 56a:22:1.hebrew: חזקתו בדוק - מי מחזקינן דבדיק ליה בשעת הכיבוד, ומשום הכי טהרות דקודם כיבוד טהורות:
Rashi on Niddah 56a:22:1.english: Its presumption is [that it was] examined - Do we presume that one examined it at the time of the sweeping, and because of this, [ritually] pure items from before the sweeping are pure?

Rashi on Niddah 56a:22:2.hebrew: או משום דחזקתו מתכבד - דאי הוה התם בשעת כיבוד, הוי נפיק האי שרץ מחמת כיבוד:
Rashi on Niddah 56a:22:2.english: Or because its presumptive status is that it is swept - For had it been there at the time of the sweeping, this creeping animal would have gone out on account of the sweeping.

Rashi on Niddah 56a:23:1.hebrew: דאמר כביד ולא בדיק - כבדתיו ולא בדקתיו. אי אמרת דהא דמטהרין הנך דמקמי כיבוד משום דחזקתו שבדקו בשעת כיבוד, הא לא בדיק, וטהרות דמקמי כיבוד נמי טמאו'. ואי אמרת כו':
Rashi on Niddah 56a:23:1.english: Where he said: Swept and not examined - [Meaning:] "I swept it, but I did not examine it." If you say that the reason we deem pure those [items] prior to the sweeping is because the presumption is that he examined it at the time of sweeping, behold, he did not examine [it], and the pure items prior to the sweeping are also impure. And if you say, etc.

Rashi on Niddah 56a:2:1.hebrew: דם היוצא מפי אמתו - של זב גמור, יליף ליה לקמן דטהור:
Rashi on Niddah 56a:2:1.english: Blood that emerges from the opening of his penis - [That] of a full-fledged zav, [the Gemara] derives below that it is pure.

Rashi on Niddah 56a:2:2.hebrew: יכול דם היוצא מפיו - של זב יהא נדון כרוק, ודם היוצא מפי אמתו יהא נדון כזוב:
Rashi on Niddah 56a:2:2.english: One might [think] blood that issues from his mouth - [That] of a zav should be judged like saliva, and blood that issues from the opening of his penis should be judged like zov.

Rashi on Niddah 56a:3:1.hebrew: ואיפוך אנא - וזאת לרבות דם, והוא להוציא מי רגלים:
Rashi on Niddah 56a:3:1.english: And let me reverse [it] - "And this" [comes] to include blood, and "it" [comes] to exclude urine.

Rashi on Niddah 56a:3:2.hebrew: שמתעגל - מתאסף הרבה כאחד, ואח"כ יוצא, כגון רוק, ומי רגלים, ושכבת זרע. דם אין מתעגל ויוצא, דכי אתא, קמא קמא נפיק:
Rashi on Niddah 56a:3:2.english: That gathers together - A large amount collects together and afterwards emerges, such as saliva, urine, and semen. Blood does not gather together and emerge, for as it comes, each bit emerges as it arrives.

Rashi on Niddah 56a:5:1.english: And is reabsorbed - When one does not emit it.

Rashi on Niddah 56a:6:1.hebrew: אף כל כו' - כגון סילון של מי רגלים, חוזר ונבלע. יצא דם, שאינו מתעגל ויוצא. חלב, אע"ג שמתעגל, אינו חוזר ונבלע:
Rashi on Niddah 56a:6:1.english: So too, all, etc. - Such as a stream of urine, [which] is reabsorbed. Blood is excluded, as it does not gather together and emerge; [and] milk, even though it gathers together, is not reabsorbed.

Rashi on Niddah 56a:7:1.english: And its skeleton - The outline of its form.

Rashi on Niddah 56a:7:2.english: Intact - That it was not broken and scattered.

Rashi on Niddah 56a:7:3.hebrew: בכולן - בשכולו שלם, טמא אפילו יבש:
Rashi on Niddah 56a:7:3.english: In all of them - Where all of it is intact, it is impure even [when] dry.

Rashi on Niddah 56a:8:1.english: Them - Regarding creeping animals, it is written (Leviticus 11:26): "Whoever touches them."

Rashi on Niddah 56a:8:2.english: Of them - "And upon whatever any of them falls when they are dead shall be impure" (ibid.).

Tosafot on Niddah 56a:10:1.hebrew: שרץ שנשרף - ק"ק דלא עריב יבש ושרוף בהדי הדדי, דמחד קרא קדריש להו:
Tosafot on Niddah 56a:10:1.english: A creeping animal that was burned - It is somewhat difficult [to understand] why he did not combine [a] dry and [a] burned [creeping animal] together, since he expounds them from a single verse.

Tosafot on Niddah 56a:15:1.hebrew: שכבת זרע בראויה להזריע - ואם תאמר: והלא שכבת זרע שאינו יורה כחץ אינו ראוי להזריע, ומטמא? ויש לומר, דמין ראוי להזריע בעינן; ואפי' שאינו יורה כחץ, כיון שהוא לח, חשיב מין שכבת זרע הראוי להזריע:
Tosafot on Niddah 56a:15:1.english: Semen, [only] when it is fit to inseminate - And if you say: But behold, semen that does not shoot like an arrow is not fit to inseminate, and [yet] it transmits impurity? And one can say that we require a type [of substance] that is fit to inseminate; and even [semen] that does not shoot like an arrow, since it is moist, is considered a type of semen that is fit to inseminate.

Tosafot on Niddah 56a:1:1.hebrew: דם היוצא מפיו טהור - בפרק מצות חליצה (יבמות דף קה.) מוקי בשותת, דאי לאו הכי טמא משום צחצוחי הרוק:
Tosafot on Niddah 56a:1:1.english: Blood that issues from his mouth is pure - In the chapter [entitled] 'Mitzvat Chalitzah' (Yevamot 105a), [the Gemara] establishes [it as referring to blood that] flows, for if not so, it would be impure on account of the droplets of saliva.

Tosafot on Niddah 56a:1:2.hebrew: דם היוצא מפי האמה - ואם תאמר: הא כבר ממעטינן בריש בנות כותים (לעיל נדה דף לב:) איש מאודם? ויש לומר: דהיינו דאין נעשה זב ע"י ראיית אודם; אבל אם כבר נעשה זב, ליהוי דם היוצא מפי האמה טמא כמו רוקו, ולכך צריך קרא הכא למעוטי:
Tosafot on Niddah 56a:1:2.english: Blood that issues from the opening of the penis - And if you say: But didn't we already exclude, at the beginning of [the chapter] "Benot Kutim" (above, Niddah 32b), "a man from red [discharge]"? And one can say: That [exclusion means only] that he does not become a zav through seeing red [discharge]; but if he has already become a zav, let the blood that issues from the opening of the penis be impure like his saliva! And therefore, a verse is needed here to exclude [it].

Tosafot on Niddah 56a:1:3.hebrew: וזאת לרבות מימי רגליו לטומאה - מוי"ו דוזאת קדריש, כי היכי דדרשינן לעיל כיחו וניעו מוי"ו דוכי ירוק. אבל זאת בכל דוכתי אתא למעוטי; והאי זאת נמי אתא למעוטי, דבת"כ מצריך תרי מיעוטי, זאת וטמא הוא — חד למעוטי זיעה וליחה סרוחה, וחד למעוטי דם היוצא מפיו ומפי האמה:
Tosafot on Niddah 56a:1:3.english: "And this" to include his urine with regard to impurity - He expounds [this inclusion] from the vav of ve-zot ("and this"), just as we expounded above [regarding] his phlegm and his mucus from the vav of ve-khi yaroq ("and if [the zav] spits"). But [the word] zot ("this") everywhere comes to exclude, and this zot also comes to exclude; for in Torat Kohanim, it requires two exclusions, zot and tamei hu ("it is impure") — one to exclude sweat and foul secretions, and one to exclude blood that issues from his mouth and from the opening of the penis.

Tosafot on Niddah 56a:3:1.hebrew: מה רוק שמתעגל ויוצא כו' - מכח ריבויא דוכי ירוק הזב בטהור ודוזאת דריש הכי. אבל אי לאו הני קראי, הוה ממעטינן כולהו: כיחו וניעו ומי רגלים, מטמא הוא, כמו דם היוצא מפי האמה. וא"ת: ולמה לי תרי קראי, וכי ירוק לכיחו וניעו וזאת למי רגלים? וי"ל, דמוכי ירוק לא הוה דרשינן אלא כיחו וניעו שיוצא דרך הפה, או מי האף נמי לרבי יוחנן, דדמי כמו רוק; ומוזאת לא הוה מרבינן אלא מי רגלים שיוצאין מפי האמה, כמו זוב, דקרא דוזאת גבי זוב כתיב, או משום דבאין ממקום טמא. מיהו קשה, דמשמע דהוה מרבינן חלב האשה מוזאת אם היה חוזר ונבלע; ואמאי? והא אפילו כיחו וניעו לא הוה מתרבי מוזאת אי לאו ריבויא דוכי ירוק! וצריך לומר, דאי לאו ריבויא דוכי ירוק, הוה מוקמינן וזאת לכיחו וניעו דוקא, דהוי כעין רוק; אבל השתא דכתיב וכי ירוק, אייתר וזאת לכל דבר המתעגל ויוצא וחוזר ונבלע:
Tosafot on Niddah 56a:3:1.english: Just as saliva gathers together and comes out, etc. - It is by virtue of the amplification of "And if the zav spit upon him that is clean" (Leviticus 15:8) and of "and this" (Leviticus 15:3) that [the Gemara] expounds this. But if not for these verses, we would have excluded all of them — his phlegm, and his mucus, and urine — from "it is impure" (Leviticus 15:2), just like blood that issues from the opening of the penis. And if you say: Why do I need two verses: "and if [he] spits" for his phlegm and his mucus, and "and this" for urine? And one can say that from "and if [he] spits" we would only have derived his phlegm and his mucus, which exit via the mouth (or also nasal fluids according to Rabbi Yoḥanan), as they are similar to saliva; and from "and this" we would only have included urine, which exits from the opening of the penis like zov, as the verse of "and this" is written regarding zov, or because it comes from an impure place. However, it is difficult: For it implies that we would have included a woman's milk from "and this" if it were reabsorbed. But why? Even his phlegm and his mucus would not have been included from "and this" if not for the amplification of "and if [he] spits"! And one must say that if not for the amplification of "and if [he] spits," we would have applied "and this" to his phlegm and his mucus specifically, as they are like saliva; but now that "and if [he] spits" is written, "and this" is superfluous [and available to include] anything that gathers together and comes out, and is reabsorbed.

Tosafot on Niddah 56a:6:1.hebrew: ונילף מזובו - אי זיבה לאו מעין הוה, דבעיא היא בפרק בנות כותים (לעיל נדה לד:):
Tosafot on Niddah 56a:6:1.english: And let us derive from his zivah - [This applies] if zivah is not [considered] a source (ma'ayan), as it is a dilemma in the chapter [entitled] "Benot Kutim" (above, Niddah 34b).

Tosafot on Niddah 56a:9:1.hebrew: אי בהם אי מהם כו' - ואע"ג דמהאי בהם ומהם דרשינן בפ"ק דחגיגה (דף יא.) ששיעורו בכעדשה, התם אסמכתא הוא, דשיעורים הלכה למשה מסיני:
Tosafot on Niddah 56a:9:1.english: If "them", if "of them", etc. - And even though from this [phrase of] "them" and "of them" we derive in the first chapter of Chagigah (11a) that its measure is a lentil's bulk (ke'adashah), there it is [merely] an asmachta (biblical support), for [halakhic] measurements are a Halakha le-Moshe mi-Sinai (a law given to Moses at Sinai).
